messages.text: Man Utd beware! Malen is a man transformed at Roma

metadata.summary: The top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 is not Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe, not Erling Haaland or Lamine Yamal. That honour belongs to Donyell Malen. A revelation at Roma, he makes his return to England against Manchester United on Tuesday night.
metadata.content: Donyell Malen at Roma: Man Utd face the top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 with the Dutchman transformed | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Donyell Malen at Roma: Man Utd face the top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 with the Dutchman transformed Donyell Malen has been on fire in front of goal for Roma since signing from Aston Villa and that makes him the last man Manchester United want to face in the Champions League. Adam Bate examines the transformation of the Netherlands international in Italy Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 3 November 2026 10:41, UK Image: Roma forward Donyell Malen is a man transformed since arriving in Serie A The top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 is not Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe, not Erling Haaland or Lamine Yamal. That honour belongs to Donyell Malen. A revelation at Roma, he makes his return to England against Manchester United on Tuesday night. Malen was a popular figure at Aston Villa but even his biggest admirers might not have anticipated all this. Fourteen goals in 18 Serie A games on loan last season certainly suggested that Roma could get the best from him but Malen has gone to another level. messages.text: Hamilton calls for 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Leclerc incident

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton reiterated "something needs to change" after his latest incident with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc cost the Scuderia victory in Mexico; watch Friday's practice sessions in Brazil from 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Tuesday 3 November 2026 06:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle feels Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's squabbling during the Mexico City GP cost them a one-two finish Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given. Leclerc attacked Hamilton around the outside going into Turn 4 but outbraked himself and cut the corner to take the lead, while Hamilton lost out to Red Bull's Max Verstappen after briefly going off track. The stewards gave Leclerc a five-second time penalty which allowed Verstappen to overtake him during the pit stop phase, going on to win the race while Hamilton finished second and Leclerc in fourth. Thierno Barry's second-half goal earned Everton a 1-0 win at St James' Park and their first away victory in the Premier League this season, as Newcastle were booed off at half-time and full-time following their fourth defeat in five games across all competitions.
